title: 1994 AHSME Problem 28
statement: In the \(xy\)-plane, how many lines whose \(x\)-intercept is a positive prime number and whose \(y\)-intercept is a positive integer pass through the point \((4,3)?\)

solutions.text: Let the \(x\)-intercept be the prime \(p\) and the \(y\)-intercept be the positive integer \(q.\) Intercept form gives \[ \begin{gathered} \frac4p+\frac3q=1, \\ q=\frac{3p}{p-4}=3+\frac{12}{p-4}. \end{gathered} \] Thus \(p-4\) is a positive divisor of \(12.\) Testing \(1,2,3,4,6,12\) gives prime \(p\) only for \(p=5\) and \(p=7.\) Therefore there are \(2\) lines. Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: Let the intercepts be \(p\) and \(q\), and use \(\frac{4}{p}+\frac{3}{q}=1\)
